exams.replay_evidence: Arven had already selected Buddy-Buddy Poffin, but its Tool window is observed before either searched card enters hand; active Shaymin and an empty bench therefore need a source-bound Poffin plus TM Evolution macro.
Secret Box selected TM Devolution while Snorunt and Impidimp development was still incomplete; TM Evolution was the live Tool that advanced both engines.
The live prompt exposed energy Impidimp, Snorunt, and zero-energy Impidimp but only the first option was selected. The legal two-target route is Snorunt plus the energy-bearing Marnie root.
TM Evolution must preserve physical entity cardinality when two different Snorunt share the same printing UID.
Evolving a zero-energy Morgrem prevents Punk Up from completing that line, so Snorunt and the energy-bearing Impidimp must take the two slots.
From the second own turn onward Budew no longer advances setup and is a 30-damage prize liability; the only useful Poffin target here is Snorunt.
Poffin is optional and must return no target when only late Budew remains.
Late Artazon must reserve the bench for Munkidori damage transfer rather than a fresh Budew.
Artazon selection is optional and must not consume the last bench slot with a late Budew.
With Impidimp in play and no Rare Candy, recovering Stage-2 Grimmsnarl is dead; Morgrem enables immediate legal evolution and keeps Punk Up available.
Punk Up must assign the remaining Darkness to the one-Energy Marnie Pokemon and stop at exactly two instead of funding Munkidori.
A legal Froslass evolution is a permanent pre-attack engine action and must precede a nonterminal Shadow Bullet.
With Impidimp present and no Morgrem, the public Spikemuth bridge must execute before a nonterminal attack.
Once Froslass is online, a Darkness-funded Munkidori is the highest-value single-prize handoff and Budew is a prize liability.
A legal Iono must refill a depleted hand and disrupt a large opposing hand before a nonterminal attack.
With Budew active, Impidimp and Snorunt established, and the manual attachment still open, Arven must secure TM Evolution before optional Munkidori funding.
A live Morgrem plus Snorunt is an immediate two-target TM Evolution transaction, so Rescue Board cannot take the tool slot while both engines are incomplete.
Two live Snorunt and no Froslass make TM Evolution the core-completing Secret Box tool; TM Devolution is not a substitute.
Once TM Evolution is in hand and a Snorunt is live, the zero-Energy active must receive the manual Darkness before an optional Munkidori.
An Energy-bearing Morgrem may be evolved safely and completes Grimmsnarl alongside one Froslass; the optional Munkidori line cannot displace either core target.
Immediately before TM Evolution, manually evolving the zero-Energy Impidimp into Morgrem destroys the second valid target and recreates the forbidden zero-Energy Morgrem choice.
The live bench host exposes TM Evolution as attack_target with max two, not effect_target; both Impidimp and Snorunt must be selected.
The first player cannot attack on global turn one. Attaching TM Evolution here discards it unused at end of turn and destroys the next-turn double-evolution line.
Froslass is online, Munkidori is in hand, the bench has space, and the attack is nonterminal. Munkidori must enter play before attacking so Adrena-Brain is available on the following turn.
With active Budew, two Impidimp, Arven, and the only Darkness attachment, funding Impidimp first leaves the later TM Evolution unusable. Fund the active before resolving the Arven-Poffin-TM chain.
The first Froslass and Grimmsnarl are online, a second Froslass is in hand over live Snorunt, and the attack does not end the game. Complete the second damage engine before attacking.
With two cards in hand, six prizes remaining versus two, and an eleven-card opposing hand, a two-prize knockout is not terminal. Arven must develop resources before the same attack remains available.
Spikemuth exposed two Grimmsnarl while Morgrem was already in hand and Impidimp remained active, but the policy selected a redundant Impidimp and broke the next-turn evolution chain.
The live Night Stretcher prompt was effect_target. With no Grimmsnarl evolution bridge on board or in hand, the policy recovered late Budew although Impidimp was available.

After Budew was knocked out, promoting the funded Impidimp exposed the only live Morgrem bridge and it was knocked out before Grimmsnarl could evolve. Promote the zero-Energy Munkidori and preserve the invested line on the Bench.

The live TM Evolution attack_target window identifies the attacking Morgrem as source_uid while max_count remains two. The old count rule looked for TM Evolution as source_uid, missed, and returned only one target.

The manual attachment was still available and two damaged Munkidori were in play, but only one had Darkness Energy. Arven treated every Item as zero-value and took Counter Catcher; Energy Search immediately starts the second Adrena-Brain transfer for another 30 damage before the attack.

Arven had fetched Energy Search and the manual attachment was still available. After the first Munkidori transfer, the policy used Artazon and ended the turn, leaving the second damaged Munkidori unfunded until the next turn. Energy Search must complete the same-turn transfer chain before Stadium or end-turn actions.

TM Evolution was in hand, the active Impidimp was funded, and the Bench exposed both Snorunt and another Impidimp. Manually evolving Snorunt first reduced the live TM window to one target. Attach TM first so it can evolve both the Snorunt and the backup Impidimp.

A funded active Impidimp, a Benched Snorunt, a second Impidimp, and TM Evolution in hand already formed a two-target TM chain. Arven chose Ultra Ball, which immediately pulled Froslass out of the deck and made the Snorunt target unable to evolve. Choose Energy Search and leave both Froslass and Morgrem in the deck for TM Evolution.

With Budew active and Impidimp plus Snorunt already on the Bench, Arven's Tool half could fetch TM Evolution next. Choosing Ultra Ball first removed Morgrem from the deck, so the following TM attack evolved only Snorunt. Choose Energy Search and preserve both Morgrem and Froslass as live deck evolutions.

The prior winning trajectory selected Night Stretcher from Arven when the Item window had no Ultra Ball. The broad TM-preservation rule incorrectly replaced it with Energy Search and turned the same seeded game into a loss. Energy Search may replace Ultra Ball, but must not replace Night Stretcher when Ultra Ball is absent.

Morgrem was active with one Darkness Energy while Grimmsnarl and another Darkness Energy were in hand. Two spare Impidimp and Munkidori were legal retreat targets. Ending the turn exposed Morgrem to the next Ogerpon attachment and knockout; retreat to a spare Impidimp, then attach before evolving Morgrem next turn.

Morgrem will evolve from hand, so Punk Up can fill the resulting Marnie's Grimmsnarl to exactly two Darkness Energy without spending the manual attachment first. The manual attachment belongs on non-Marnie's Munkidori, which Punk Up can never fund.

After Poffin benched two Snorunt, active Grimmsnarl had exactly two Darkness Energy and TM Evolution was in hand. The policy gave the ordinary attack 21001 versus only 18500 for attaching TM Evolution, attacked immediately, and left both Snorunt unevolved.

After correctly funding Morgrem before evolution, Munkidori remained at zero energy. On turn 7 manual attachment and supporter were both live, no Darkness Energy was in hand, Professor's Research was available, and the only attack projected zero active damage. The policy attacked instead of refreshing the hand to find Munkidori's missing energy.

Professor's Research found Darkness Energy, but after re-observation the policy scored attaching it to zero-energy Munkidori at 31500 and the zero-active-damage attack at 32000, so it attacked for a 500-point margin. The newly found energy must be attached before attacking.

At 2 prizes versus the opponent's 1, active Munkidori had one Darkness Energy and two Darkness Energy were in hand. Iono scored 192500 and was played before the zero-score attachment, shuffling both energies away and preventing the final attack. Attach to two first, then Iono and re-observe.

With only three cards in hand, two unevolved Snorunt, no Froslass and no Munkidori, the policy scored Professor's Research at zero and attacked for 180. Research can be played first without consuming the attack and should refresh the missing engine pieces.

Fresh active Grimmsnarl ex had two Darkness Energy and no Tool, the opposing active Crustle was evolved, and Shadow Bullet projected zero active damage. TM Devolution was in hand, but the policy ended the turn instead of attaching it and opening the granted devolution attack.

After the corrected TM Devolution attachment and Froslass evolution, the granted devolution attack was a legal current-window option. The public damage planner inferred 180 current attack damage even though the protected normal attack option projected zero; the over-specific zero-damage condition therefore missed, the granted attack scored zero, and the policy ended instead of completing the devolution line.

Active Impidimp could attack for only 10 while a fully funded, attack-ready Grimmsnarl ex was on the Bench and retreat remained available. The one-point positive-damage fallback beat the zero-score retreat, so the policy used the weak attack and skipped both the ready attacker and the re-observed development window.

Shadow Bullet had two single-prize Bench targets: a 70-HP Dwebble and a 50-HP evolved Crustle. With Froslass already in play, the policy had no target rule and chose Dwebble by index. The 30 Bench damage belongs on the lower-HP Crustle so subsequent Froslass checks complete the knockout route.

Active Morgrem had two Darkness Energy and a 60-damage attack into a 20-HP two-prize Ogerpon. The only other Pokémon was an already evolved Froslass, so TM Evolution could not provide two valid evolution targets. The policy attached TM Evolution and used an empty granted attack instead of taking the guaranteed two prizes.

Two Impidimp and one Snorunt were already deployed, but the active was Munkidori rather than the early Budew TM Evolution pivot. The broad preserve-TM rule forced Energy Search over Buddy-Buddy Poffin and opened the first trajectory regression. Keep the Energy Search override scoped to the live active-Budew TM line.

The active was Snorunt with two Impidimp on the Bench and no active Budew TM Evolution pivot. Rejecting Ultra Ball here made Arven take a score-zero filler item. The Ultra Ball rejection must share the same active-Budew scope as its paired Energy Search preference.

At turn 31 the board was already full, Grimmsnarl and one Froslass were online, and adding a second Froslass only increased between-turn damage to the strategy's own Ability Pokemon. The attack-before-development rule is an opening and midgame completion rule, not unconditional late-game authority.

Night Stretcher offered Darkness Energy and Morgrem while the only live Impidimp had zero Energy. Taking Morgrem would create exactly the zero-energy TM evolution liability the strategy forbids; recover Darkness Energy first so Munkidori or the Marnie line can be funded.

Grimmsnarl was online but Shadow Bullet projected zero Active damage into the wall, no Froslass was in play, and Iono was still available. Attacking first only placed Bench chip and left the development supporter unused; Iono must refresh the six-card hand and disrupt before this nonterminal attack.

The active Grimmsnarl had only 80 HP left, Munkidori was deployed without Darkness Energy, Energy Search was in hand, and the manual attachment remained available. Resolve Energy Search before the nonterminal Shadow Bullet so Munkidori can be funded and move damage before the turn ends.

Shadow Bullet projected zero Active damage into Crustle while two full two-prize Ogerpon sat on the Bench. Boss's Orders was available but scored below the empty wall attack. Gust a two-prize Ogerpon before attacking so the attack creates prize progress instead of only incidental Bench chip.

Night Stretcher offered Impidimp and Morgrem while both live Impidimp had zero Darkness Energy; the only Darkness Energy was on Munkidori. Recovering Morgrem incorrectly treated that unrelated Energy as a funded evolution bridge and changed a baseline win into a loss; keep the basic Impidimp until its own line is funded.

A Benched Impidimp already had two Darkness Energy and Morgrem was in hand. The active Grimmsnarl could take two prizes but not end the game, so evolving the fully funded backup first was free development that the attack permanently skipped.

Active Impidimp could deal only 10 damage to a one-prize target while legal Counter Catcher exposed a damaged two-prize Ogerpon without increasing the public attack-window count. The old no-attacker penalty hid the strictly better prize route and attacked immediately.

The candidate matched the winning baseline through turn 24, then used Boss while active Grimmsnarl still had only one Dark Energy. The zero-damage fact described the current unfunded board, not the attack available after the manual attachment, so the broad gust rule spent the supporter before Adrena-Brain and changed the winning long-game route into a loss.

After Adrena-Brain and the manual attachment, the winning baseline ended the turn into the damaged one-prize wall. The candidate instead spent Boss to expose a two-prize Ogerpon and attacked, which changed the same-seed result from a win to a loss. With the damage engine already used, a ready backup Grimmsnarl, a four-prize versus six-prize lead, and zero Active damage, preserve the established long-game route.

Two Grimmsnarl were already fully funded, Snorunt was in play, no Froslass had been built, and the hand contained only Energy Search, Iono, and Arven. The attempted Arven repair fetched Buddy-Buddy Poffin and TM Devolution, then Poffin's only remaining target was the prohibited late Budew. Because no legal Arven Item can acquire Froslass in this public window, Iono is the executable draw route toward the missing first Froslass even though it also refills the opponent's one-card hand.

After the repaired draw line produced Grimmsnarl plus Froslass, the opponent reached one prize with seven cards in hand. The active one-energy Grimmsnarl could neither attack nor retreat into a productive action, yet the policy ended the turn while Iono was legal. Iono is the mandatory public denial checkpoint here: it reduces the opponent from seven cards to one and preserves a final defensive turn instead of conceding with an unused supporter.

The board had no Froslass, one underfunded Grimmsnarl, an energy-bearing Morgrem ready to evolve, Snorunt, and an energy-bearing Impidimp. Spikemuth Gym was already in play and its effect was legal, but every option tied at zero so the policy ended. The owning continuity rule only handled either zero Grimmsnarl or zero Morgrem, leaving this exact one-Grimmsnarl plus one-Morgrem bridge uncovered. Use Spikemuth now to fetch the second Grimmsnarl and complete the funded evolution before passing.

Arven had completed its search, the active Grimmsnarl was ready, Snorunt was already waiting to evolve, two Bench spaces were open, and Munkidori remained in hand. The policy attached TM Devolution and then attacked for a nonterminal 180 without deploying Munkidori. Bench Munkidori before the attack so the upcoming Froslass engine has a damage mover in play and the next send-out window is not restricted to an unfunded two-prize Grimmsnarl, Snorunt, and Impidimp.

After the attacking Grimmsnarl was knocked out, the policy gave all three send-out options zero and defaulted to the first option: a zero-Energy two-prize Grimmsnarl. A two-Darkness Impidimp was already attack-ready and worth only one prize. With no funded Munkidori damage-transfer handoff available, promote the ready one-prize attacker and keep the unfunded Grimmsnarl on the Bench for later repair.

The one-Snorunt Iono recovery rule leaked into a materially different board with two Snorunt, a complete Grimmsnarl, a funded Impidimp, Munkidori, and a full Bench. It overrode Arven by 280000 to 22500 and changed an iteration-44 win into a loss. Keep Iono's forced first-Froslass refresh scoped to exactly one Snorunt; with two established evolution targets, Arven is the deterministic development route.

Active Munkidori had one Darkness Energy, manual attachment was still available, no Darkness Energy was in hand, and Energy Search was legal. Every useful action tied at zero and the policy ended, then repeated the same pass two turns later. Energy Search must resolve before ending so Munkidori reaches two Energy and can attack or preserve the damage-transfer route.

The supporter had already been spent, Munkidori was in play without Energy, no Darkness Energy was in hand, and Energy Search was legal. Although the manual attachment had already been used, Energy Search is a free pre-attack action that secures the next turn's Munkidori attachment. The policy instead took a nonterminal Shadow Bullet and lost the only chance to prepare the damage mover.

A ready Grimmsnarl and funded Morgrem were established, but no Snorunt or Froslass was in play, the hand was only four cards, Professor's Research was legal, and the opponent still had five prizes. Research scored zero while a nonterminal Shadow Bullet scored 21001, so the policy attacked without drawing toward the missing damage engine. Refresh the hand before attacking once immediate hand evolutions and TM Evolution are absent.

Budew had completed its first-turn stall job. Two Energy-bearing Impidimp and two Snorunt were already on the Bench, TM Evolution was in hand, and retreat was still available, but the policy kept Budew Active and attacked for 10 for four more turns. Retreat to a funded Impidimp first so the re-observed main window can attach TM Evolution and evolve two live targets immediately.

Active Grimmsnarl was fully funded but its Shadow Bullet projected zero damage into the current wall. TM Evolution was in hand while an Energy-bearing Morgrem and an unevolved Snorunt were both valid useful targets. The policy repeatedly chose the zero-damage attack instead of finishing Froslass plus the backup Grimmsnarl line.

At one prize each, Secret Box discarded Budew, Boss's Orders, and Rare Candy by option order. Grimmsnarl was recoverable from the discard and another Rare Candy remained in hand, so Boss had to be preserved for the next-turn final-prize gust. Discard expendable Budew, Research, and one redundant Rare Candy instead.

Secret Box could take Night Stretcher while Grimmsnarl was in the discard and Rare Candy was still in hand, creating an immediate active Grimmsnarl plus Punk Up route. It selected Super Rod instead, which only recycled the attacker into the deck and delayed the line until turn 31.

Research had already converted both Snorunt into Froslass and benched Munkidori, but the active one-Energy Froslass could not attack. Two exactly funded Marnie attackers were available on the Bench and retreat was unused, yet the policy ended the turn and gave up all post-development tempo. Retreat into the ready Grimmsnarl ex before ending so development is followed by the best legal attack window.

Active Impidimp already had the Energy needed to use TM Evolution, and both Snorunt plus the second Impidimp were useful evolution targets. The policy spent Energy Search and the manual attachment on an optional Munkidori first, losing the active Impidimp before the evolution attack. Attach TM Evolution to the funded active holder before optional Munkidori funding while the core is incomplete.

The only Munkidori already had one Dark Energy, which is sufficient for Adrena-Brain. With no other useful manual attachment and Shadow Bullet doing zero into the wall, Energy Search created a redundant Energy that could not be attached and delayed the actual core-development draw. Do not spend Energy Search merely because Munkidori has attack Energy debt when its transfer Ability is already funded.

After the only Grimmsnarl was Knocked Out, two Snorunt and a Munkidori with one Dark Energy remained. The policy sent out a zero-Energy Snorunt, evolved it Active, and lost that Froslass before it could establish the damage engine. Send out the already funded Munkidori so the next Froslass evolution immediately enables Adrena-Brain and preserves both Snorunt as Bench damage sources.

Active Munkidori had only one Energy and no useful attack while a fully funded Grimmsnarl ex was ready on the Bench. Retreat was unused, but the policy ended the turn and repeated the pass across multiple turns until the opponent took the game. Retreat to the ready Grimmsnarl before ending so the completed Marnie attacker actually converts setup into prize pressure.

A damaged, fully funded Grimmsnarl ex and a live Froslass were already in play while Munkidori and Darkness Energy were both in hand. The policy spent Arven first even though the transfer package was already complete, making the supporter unavailable before Munkidori was benched and funded. Bench Munkidori first so the public turn can bind the Energy and Adrena-Brain actions before choosing the draw supporter.

The opponent had one Prize remaining and eleven cards in hand. Grimmsnarl ex could not damage the Active wall, but a funded Munkidori was preserved and a one-attack two-Prize gust target existed. Professor's Research was legal with enough deck remaining and could find Counter Catcher or TM Devolution; the policy instead ended the turn and conceded the last uncontested Prize. Use the supporter before accepting a zero-damage terminal pass.

Active Munkidori had one Darkness Energy, eight damage counters, and a live Froslass, so Adrena-Brain could move three counters immediately. A ready Grimmsnarl ex was on the Bench. The policy retreated first, discarding Munkidori's Darkness Energy and invalidating the available transfer window. Use Adrena-Brain before retreating; the following reobserved window may then pivot into Grimmsnarl.

After Adrena-Brain moved three counters, Active Munkidori remained a low-HP one-Prize Pokemon while a ready Grimmsnarl ex waited on the Bench. Retreating discarded Munkidori's only Darkness Energy and exposed the two-Prize attacker immediately. Preserve the funded one-Prize handoff; if it is Knocked Out, Grimmsnarl enters without paying the retreat resource.

Grimmsnarl ex, Froslass, and a funded Munkidori were already deployed, but the Active wall reduced Grimmsnarl's damage to zero. Iono was legal from a three-card hand. The policy chose the zero-active-damage Shadow Bullet chip and then repeated zero-damage passes over several turns. Use Iono first to rebuild the hand and search for Counter Catcher, Boss's Orders, or TM Devolution before accepting the wall line.

After Adrena-Brain, the only funded Munkidori remained Active at 90 HP while a second Munkidori was in hand, but no Darkness Energy was available to activate that backup. Deploying the naked backup before Arven consumed the last Bench space and produced no transfer window; the same pattern regressed seeds 2919028 and 2919046. Keep the supporter route unless the backup Munkidori can be funded in the same public turn.

On the second own turn, Budew remained Active while two attack-ready Impidimp were already funded on the Bench. With the emergency first-turn stall window over, the policy still used Budew's ten-damage attack and repeated that low-pressure line for several turns. Retreat the zero-cost Budew into a funded Marnie Pokemon so evolution and prize-pressure turns are no longer delayed.

Budew was Active as a one-Prize buffer, but a fully funded Grimmsnarl ex, a live Froslass line, and Munkidori were already established behind it. The broad second-turn handoff rule retreated into Grimmsnarl and turned the prior win into a loss. Once the core attacker already exists, preserve Budew's single-Prize buffer instead of exposing the two-Prize attacker merely to satisfy the early handoff heuristic.

Active Munkidori could retreat into a ready Grimmsnarl ex, but Spikemuth was unused and two Snorunt were still unevolved while Froslass was in hand. The retreat rule took authority first and the former win became a loss. Complete the stadium search and Froslass development in fresh windows before consuming the retreat and exposing the two-Prize attacker.

Active Munkidori and a ready Grimmsnarl ex were present, but only three Pokemon were deployed and Artazon was still in hand. The retreat rule exposed Grimmsnarl before using the open Bench and the former win became a loss. Play Artazon first, reobserve, and finish the missing Snorunt line before deciding whether to retreat.

After a Knock Out on turn six, a fully funded Grimmsnarl ex and a one-Energy Munkidori were both available. The late-transfer send-out rule already treated Munkidori as the highest priority even though no Froslass was live, and the former win became a loss. Before the late transfer phase, send out the ready attacker; reserve funded-Munkidori priority for turn nine or later.

TM Evolution opened a live two-target attack window containing a two-Dark Morgrem and a Snorunt. Because the fixed-count rule was incorrectly bound to TM Evolution as the window source while the real engine reported the attacking Grimmsnarl ex, the policy fell back to desired_count=1 and evolved only Morgrem. Select both useful targets so the same attack also establishes Froslass; the Energy-bearing guard must continue to exclude a zero-Energy Morgrem.

The active Grimmsnarl ex had only one Energy and no attack, while the only legal progress action was Professor's Research. The policy assigned no rule to either Research and ended the turn with a four-card hand. Use the supporter to find attachment, transfer, recovery, or gust resources before accepting a zero-damage pass.

A funded active Munkidori and an unevolved Snorunt were already present with Froslass in hand while the opponent had two Prizes left. The policy ended the turn and never activated the damage-transfer engine. Evolve Froslass first so future between-turn counters can be converted into multi-target prize pressure.

A two-Dark Impidimp was ready for the Grimmsnarl line and Spikemuth was unused, but the score of the TM Devolution granted attack won the window immediately. Stadium development does not consume the attack, so use Spikemuth first, reobserve, and only then take the attack.

After Adrena-Brain had already moved the available counters, a healthy one-Energy Active Munkidori and a live Froslass still formed the late single-Prize transfer handoff. The broad retreat rule discarded Munkidori's Darkness Energy and exposed a two-Prize Grimmsnarl ex. Preserve Munkidori when Froslass is online; the no-Froslass turn-seven exam continues to own the real attack-conversion retreat.

Active Munkidori had one Darkness Energy, two Darkness Energy were in hand, and a ready Grimmsnarl ex waited on the Bench. The broad retreat rule discarded Munkidori's Energy before the manual attachment, even though the opposing wall left Grimmsnarl at zero Active damage. Fund Munkidori to two first and preserve the single-Prize attacker; only use the no-Energy-in-hand retreat route when this attachment is unavailable.

At two Prizes each, the candidate had only three cards, the opponent had four, no Grimmsnarl or Froslass remained in play, and the Active Impidimp could deal only ten damage. Arven scored above Iono even though Iono immediately refilled the hand and denied the opponent's final two-Prize turn. Use Iono before the nonterminal weak attack; the low-prize disruption checkpoint has higher value than an ordinary development search here.

TM Evolution was already attached, but Froslass was in hand over a live Snorunt and the granted attack was nonterminal. The turn route added 180000 authority to the granted attack and treated it as a terminal step, overriding the permanent Froslass evolution. Evolve Froslass first, reobserve, and only then decide whether the remaining TM attack has useful targets.

Active Grimmsnarl could deal 180 but not Knock Out the opposing two-Prize attacker. The hand was Research plus two redundant Munkidori while two Munkidori were already in play and no Froslass remained. Research was score zero and the policy attacked immediately. Refresh toward Froslass, Darkness Energy, gust, or recovery before the nonterminal attack.

The opponent had one Prize left, Froslass was stranded Active without Energy, a fully funded Grimmsnarl waited on the Bench, retreat was unavailable, and Research was the only legal action that could find a switch, attachment, or denial route. The policy ended immediately. Use Research before conceding the final uncontested Prize.

Active Munkidori had no Energy and no attack, a fully funded Grimmsnarl was ready on the Bench, retreat was unavailable, and the hand was only three cards including Iono. Ending gave away the tempo turn. Iono must refill toward Darkness Energy, Froslass, recovery, or a switch before passing.

The main window correctly chose a retreat option whose semantic target was the fully funded Grimmsnarl ex. After the engine invalidated that window and opened the mandatory self-switch prompt, the policy lost the semantic target and fell back to the first option, an unfunded Snorunt. Rebind the ready Grimmsnarl in the current self-switch window so the retreat produces the intended attacker instead of donating a Prize.

The public turn ledger still said retreat_available because no retreat had been declared, but the current legal window contained no retreat option: Active Froslass had zero Energy and could not pay its Retreat Cost. The recovery rule treated the unused ledger as proof of an executable retreat and failed to score Research. Current-window legality is authoritative; play Research before conceding the opponent's last Prize.
